items.title: The AI Hacks Are Way Worse Than We Thought
items.summary: Have we reached the point-of-no-return for AI hacks? In recent days, a swarm of autonomous AI agents broke out of containment and executed a series of hacks–including an attempt at breaching a government database. On today's episode of In The Loop, host Ejaaz Ahamadeen unpacks the breach, the fallout, and the question everyone in AI is suddenly asking out loud: is superintelligence finally here? Or is this just the beginning of losing control?

items.title: Why Qualcomm (QCOM) Stock Is Down Today
items.summary: Shares of wireless chipmaker Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) fell 5.8% in the afternoon session after rally momentum faded, a Samsung 2nm pricing standoff left manufacturing talks drifting toward 2027, and chip stocks joined a broader tech selloff tied to rising yields.

items.title: S&P 500's Newest Member Is Monday's Biggest Loser
items.summary: Bloom Energy, which joined the index on Sept. 21, was among the biggest S&P 500 stock losers in Monday's session.

items.title: Did The Market Read Marvell Stock Right?
items.summary: Marvell Technology (MRVL) stock fell 7.3% on Monday, September 14. A $10,000 holding at the prior close was worth about $9,270 when trading ended that day. That fall is hard to explain from the company alone. Less than three weeks earlier, management had raised its revenue forecast for fiscal 2028. Did the market read Marvell stock right that Monday.

items.title: Corning (GLW) Stock Looks Undervalued As Its 452% Run Tests Fair Value
items.summary: Corning has been on a powerful multi year run, and after a mix of AI focused partnerships and a recent equity offering, the real question is how firmly its current share price rests on the cash flows the business can generate over time. With the stock now in a very different place than it was a few years ago, investors are increasingly asking whether the recent price action still lines up with what the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view of intrinsic value supports. items.title: Intel vs. Qualcomm: Which Chip Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Intel is in the middle of a dramatic turnaround with revenue growing at its fastest pace in 15 years. Qualcomm is the more profitable business today, navigating smartphone headwinds while building new growth engines in automotive and data centers.

items.title: When Should You Buy NVIDIA Stock After This Run?
items.summary: A $10,000 holding in NVIDIA (NVDA) stock three months ago was worth about $11,700 as of September 25, 2026. Yet against profits, the shares still trade near the low end of their ten-year range. If you have been waiting to buy NVIDIA, have you already missed it.

items.title: Your Micron Shares Could Swing Hundreds Of Dollars, And That Is The Calm Case
items.summary: Micron Technology (MU) stock trades near $1,082. Options expiring in roughly a year price a likely range from about $597 to about $1,963, with roughly two-in-three odds of finishing inside it. That is a huge band. Yet options expect Micron to trade calmer than it has, and the supply contracts behind management's case for steadier results cover a minority of its memory volume.
